rules.title: Residential Security Deposit Maximum Limit
rules.requirement: Landlords are generally prohibited from demanding or receiving a security deposit in excess of one month's rent, in addition to any rent for the first month, except for qualifying small landlords who may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.key_value: 1 month rent (or 2 months for qualifying small landlords)

coverage.summary: Applies to residential property used as the dwelling of the tenant.
coverage.owner_condition: Landlords who are natural persons or LLCs consisting entirely of natural persons, owning no more than two residential rental properties with a collective total of no more than four dwelling units, may charge up to two months' rent.

rules.exemptions: Does not prohibit an advance payment of six months' rent or more for a lease of six months or longer, nor mutual agreements for tenant-requested alterations. Small landlords owning 2 residential properties or 4 total units or fewer may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.quoted_span: Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: Security Deposit Return and Itemized Accounting Deadline
rules.requirement: Landlords must furnish an itemized statement indicating the basis for and amount of any security deposit received and return any remaining portion to the tenant no later than 21 calendar days after the tenant vacates the premises.

coverage.summary: Applies to residential property used as the dwelling of the tenant.
